new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Spot-checks (only one listed work, so both parts of it plus its sole primary source were checked): (1) Central Ok page, full raw export a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/tone/tonal/pitch/prosody: no statement; (2) Hughes 2009 Upper Digul Survey text (113 KB, symlinked in the tang1353 dir): no hits for stress/accent/tone/pitch/prosody/syllable; the Tangko sociolinguistic section (printed pp. 11-13) and the Appendix V wordlist carry phonetic stress marks (rendered » in the text layer, e.g. [»ta≤qo], [sE≤»Gaop]) but no analysis or statement about stress placement. Nothing missed.

sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (Gaguop, Oct-Nov 2000); 'TANGKO' section printed pp. 11-13 (name [ˈtaŋqo], ethnonym Senggaop, pop. 102, ~30% lexical similarity with Nakai) and Appendix V (printed pp. 27-37) 239-item IPA wordlist column 'Tangko / Kawemaot' carrying primary-stress marks (ˈʔɑbuɾ 'head', ˈmɛɾu 'nose', qɔˈsɛɴ 'arm', diˈjɔn 'leg', ˌtɑnˈtɑmɔn 'mouth'). The words stress/accent/tone occur nowhere in the report; no transcription note. My own rough tally of the Tangko column (observation, not a source statement): of 180 stress-marked polysyllabic tokens, 129 final-syllable, 40 penult, 9…
